```{r setup, include = FALSE}
knitr::opts_chunk$set(collapse = TRUE, comment = "#>")
library(nlmixr2lib)
library(PKNCA)
library(rxode2)
library(dplyr)
library(tidyr)
library(ggplot2)
```

# Model and source

Fratoni et al. (2025) developed human-simulated regimens (HSRs) of meropenem,
cefiderocol and tobramycin in the standardized COMBINE neutropenic murine
pneumonia model, separately for plasma and for pulmonary epithelial lining
fluid (ELF). For each drug and each matrix they fitted a one-compartment model
with first-order subcutaneous absorption and first-order elimination (WinNonlin,
nonlinear least squares, naive-pooled), and used it to design the regimens and
to compute the murine fCmax, fAUC0-24 and %fT > MIC. The six fits are
independent, so the package carries six models:

| Model | Drug | Matrix | Parameters |
|-------|------|--------|------------|
| `Fratoni_2025_meropenem_plasma_mouse` | meropenem | plasma | Table 2 |
| `Fratoni_2025_cefiderocol_plasma_mouse` | cefiderocol | plasma | Table 2 |
| `Fratoni_2025_tobramycin_plasma_mouse` | tobramycin | plasma | Table 2 |
| `Fratoni_2025_meropenem_elf_mouse` | meropenem | ELF | Table 3 |
| `Fratoni_2025_cefiderocol_elf_mouse` | cefiderocol | ELF | Table 3 |
| `Fratoni_2025_tobramycin_elf_mouse` | tobramycin | ELF | Table 3 |

* Citation: `r rxode2::rxode(readModelDb("Fratoni_2025_meropenem_plasma_mouse"))$reference`
* Article: <https://doi.org/10.1093/jac/dkae432> (open access, PMC11787888)

The plasma models predict the TOTAL plasma concentration `Cc` and carry the
murine unbound fraction `fu`, so the free concentration is `Cu = fu * Cc`. The
ELF models predict `Celf` directly; the paper treats ELF concentrations as
unbound because bronchoalveolar lavage fluid contains no albumin.

# Population

Female specific pathogen-free CD-1 mice, 6-8 weeks old (Charles River), were
made neutropenic with intraperitoneal cyclophosphamide (150 mg/kg on day -4 and
100 mg/kg on day -1) and given a predictable degree of renal impairment with
uranyl nitrate (5 mg/kg IP on day -3). They were infected intranasally with
50 uL of *Klebsiella pneumoniae* CDC 851 following the COMBINE protocol. Drug
was given as dorsal subcutaneous injections of 0.1 mL (Table 4). Groups of six
mice were sampled per time point (two retro-orbital bleeds and one terminal
cardiac puncture per mouse, with bronchoalveolar lavage at the terminal time
point); ELF concentrations were derived from lavage by urea correction. Across
the three drugs, 10 of 108 plasma and 7 of 78 lavage samples were excluded as
interquartile-range outliers. The number of mice per drug is not reported.

The same information is available programmatically, e.g.
`readModelDb("Fratoni_2025_tobramycin_plasma_mouse")()$population`.

# Source trace

Every `ini()` value carries an in-file comment naming its source. The table
collects them.

| Model | Parameter | Value | Source location |
|-------|-----------|-------|-----------------|
| meropenem plasma | `lka` | log(1.34) 1/h | Table 2, Ka |
| meropenem plasma | `lkel` | log(27.13) 1/h | Table 2, Kel |
| meropenem plasma | `lvc` | log(0.04) L/kg | Table 2, V plasma |
| meropenem plasma | `fu` | 0.92 | Materials and methods: murine binding 8% (DeRyke 2007) |
| cefiderocol plasma | `lka` | log(21.71) 1/h | Table 2, Ka |
| cefiderocol plasma | `lkel` | log(0.74) 1/h | Table 2, Kel |
| cefiderocol plasma | `lvc` | log(0.19) L/kg | Table 2, V plasma |
| cefiderocol plasma | `fu` | 0.684 | Materials and methods: murine binding 31.6% (Monogue 2017) |
| tobramycin plasma | `lka` | log(23.68) 1/h | Table 2, Ka |
| tobramycin plasma | `lkel` | log(0.31) 1/h | Table 2, Kel |
| tobramycin plasma | `lvc` | log(0.37) L/kg | Table 2, V plasma |
| tobramycin plasma | `fu` | 0.776 | Results, ex vivo protein binding: mean 22.4% bound |
| meropenem ELF | `lka` | log(7.00) 1/h | Table 3, Ka-ELF |
| meropenem ELF | `lkeff_elf` | log(2.50) 1/h | Table 3, Kel-ELF |
| meropenem ELF | `lv_elf` | log(1.60) L/kg | Table 3, V ELF |
| cefiderocol ELF | `lka` | log(1.94) 1/h | Table 3, Ka-ELF |
| cefiderocol ELF | `lkeff_elf` | log(0.72) 1/h | Table 3, Kel-ELF |
| cefiderocol ELF | `lv_elf` | log(0.33) L/kg | Table 3, V ELF |
| tobramycin ELF | `lka` | log(1.74) 1/h | Table 3, Ka-ELF |
| tobramycin ELF | `lkeff_elf` | log(0.35) 1/h | Table 3, Kel-ELF |
| tobramycin ELF | `lv_elf` | log(0.79) L/kg | Table 3, V ELF |
| all | `propSd` | 0 (held at zero) | not reported (least-squares fit) |
| plasma | `d/dt(depot) = -ka*depot`; `d/dt(central) = ka*depot - kel*central`; `Cc = central/vc` | n/a | Results: 'one-compartment pharmacokinetic models with first order elimination'; Table 2 footnote |
| ELF | `d/dt(depot) = -ka*depot`; `d/dt(elf) = ka*depot - keff_elf*elf`; `Celf = elf/v_elf` | n/a | Results; Table 3 footnote ('absorption rate constant into ELF compartment') |
| plasma | `Cu = fu * Cc` | n/a | Materials and methods: total plasma concentrations corrected to free |

# Regimens (Table 4)

The models carry no between-animal variability, so each regimen is simulated
for one typical mouse. Each model is paired with the regimen designed for its
own matrix, which is how the paper reports Figures 1-3 and Table 5. The
meropenem and cefiderocol regimens repeat every 8 h and are simulated for three
cycles (24 h); the tobramycin regimens cover 24 h.

```{r regimens}
regimens <- tibble::tribble(
  ~drug,         ~matrix,  ~dose_times,                              ~dose_amts,
  "meropenem",   "plasma", c(0, 1.25, 3.5, 6),                       c(65, 65, 45, 45),
  "meropenem",   "ELF",    c(0, 1.25, 3.5, 4.75, 6),                 c(20, 50, 30, 20, 15),
  "cefiderocol", "plasma", c(0, 1, 2, 4, 6),                         c(5, 7.5, 10, 3.5, 1),
  "cefiderocol", "ELF",    c(0, 1, 2, 4, 6),                         c(3.75, 5, 6.25, 1.75, 1),
  "tobramycin",  "plasma", c(0, 3, 6, 9),                            c(9, 4, 2, 0.5),
  "tobramycin",  "ELF",    c(0, 1.5, 3, 4.5, 6.5, 9, 12.5, 16),      c(4.8, 3.6, 2.4, 2.4, 2.7, 2.4, 1.2, 1.2)
) |>
  mutate(
    model = sprintf(
      "Fratoni_2025_%s_%s_mouse", drug,
      ifelse(matrix == "plasma", "plasma", "elf")
    ),
    treatment = paste(drug, matrix),
    # meropenem and cefiderocol regimens repeat every 8 h; tobramycin is a
    # once-daily 24 h schedule
    n_cycles = ifelse(drug == "tobramycin", 1L, 3L),
    tau = ifelse(drug == "tobramycin", 24, 8)
  )

make_events <- function(dose_times, dose_amts, n_cycles, tau, obs_cmt) {
  doses <- tibble(
    time = as.vector(outer(dose_times, (seq_len(n_cycles) - 1) * tau, "+")),
    amt = rep(dose_amts, n_cycles),
    evid = 1L,
    cmt = "depot"
  )
  obs <- tibble(
    time = seq(0, n_cycles * tau, by = 0.01),
    amt = 0,
    evid = 0L,
    cmt = obs_cmt
  )
  bind_rows(doses, obs) |>
    arrange(time, desc(evid)) |>
    mutate(id = 1L)
}
```

# Simulation

```{r simulate}
sim <- bind_rows(lapply(seq_len(nrow(regimens)), function(i) {
  r <- regimens[i, ]
  mod <- readModelDb(r$model)
  ui <- rxode2::rxode(mod)
  is_plasma <- r$matrix == "plasma"
  ev <- make_events(
    r$dose_times[[1]], r$dose_amts[[1]], r$n_cycles, r$tau,
    obs_cmt = if (is_plasma) "central" else "elf"
  )
  s <- as.data.frame(rxode2::rxSolve(ui, events = ev))
  # Free concentration: fu * total in plasma; ELF is treated as unbound
  fconc <- if (is_plasma) s$Cu else s$Celf
  tibble(
    drug = r$drug, matrix = r$matrix, treatment = r$treatment,
    tau = r$tau, n_cycles = r$n_cycles,
    id = 1L, time = s$time, fconc = fconc
  )
}))

stopifnot(
  !anyNA(sim$fconc),
  all(sim$fconc >= -1e-6 * max(sim$fconc))
)
```

# Replicate published figures

```{r figures-1-3, fig.width = 8, fig.height = 7}
# Replicates the 'Murine Simulated' curves of Figures 1 (meropenem),
# 2 (cefiderocol) and 3 (tobramycin): free plasma and ELF concentrations over
# the first dosing interval (8 h for the beta-lactams, 24 h for tobramycin).
sim |>
  filter(time <= tau, fconc > 0) |>
  mutate(drug = factor(drug, c("meropenem", "cefiderocol", "tobramycin"))) |>
  ggplot(aes(time, fconc)) +
  geom_line(linetype = "dashed") +
  facet_wrap(drug ~ matrix, scales = "free", ncol = 2) +
  scale_y_log10() +
  labs(
    x = "Time (h)", y = "Free concentration (mg/L)",
    caption = "Replicates the murine simulated curves of Figures 1-3 of Fratoni 2025."
  )
```

Against the paper's figures: the meropenem plasma curve peaks near 65-80 mg/L
after the 0 h and 1.25 h injections and falls to about 2-5 mg/L before the 6 h
dose; the meropenem ELF curve peaks near 7 mg/L after the first injection and
near 18 mg/L after the 1.25 h injection; tobramycin plasma reaches about
18 mg/L free at 0.2 h; tobramycin ELF holds near 5-7 mg/L over 2-8 h. These are
read by eye from Figures 1-3 and match the curves above.

## Table 5: %fT > MIC

```{r table-5}
mics <- 2^(0:7)

# %fT > MIC over the third 8 h dosing interval (16-24 h), where all four
# beta-lactam models are at steady state. A fine 0.01 h grid makes the
# fraction-of-grid estimate accurate to well under one percentage point.
ft_sim <- sim |>
  filter(drug != "tobramycin", time >= 16, time < 24) |>
  group_by(drug, matrix) |>
  reframe(mic = mics, ft = sapply(mics, function(m) 100 * mean(fconc > m)))

ft_paper <- tibble::tribble(
  ~drug,         ~matrix,  ~ft,
  "meropenem",   "plasma", c(100, 100, 94, 75, 55, 29, 5, 0),
  "meropenem",   "ELF",    c(78, 62, 43, 14, 3, 0, 0, 0),
  "cefiderocol", "plasma", c(100, 100, 91, 76, 50, 16, 0, 0),
  "cefiderocol", "ELF",    c(100, 100, 85, 50, 14, 0, 0, 0)
) |>
  unnest(ft) |>
  group_by(drug, matrix) |>
  mutate(mic = mics) |>
  ungroup()

ft_cmp <- ft_sim |>
  rename(ft_sim = ft) |>
  left_join(rename(ft_paper, ft_paper = ft), by = c("drug", "matrix", "mic")) |>
  mutate(diff = ft_sim - ft_paper)

ft_cmp |>
  mutate(
    cell = sprintf("%.0f (%.0f)", ft_sim, ft_paper),
    mic = paste0("MIC ", mic)
  ) |>
  select(drug, matrix, mic, cell) |>
  pivot_wider(names_from = mic, values_from = cell) |>
  rename(Drug = drug, Matrix = matrix) |>
  knitr::kable(caption = "Simulated %fT > MIC (published mouse value from Table 5 in parentheses); MIC in mg/L.")

stopifnot(
  # Three of the four regimens reproduce Table 5 to within rounding.
  max(abs(ft_cmp$diff[!(ft_cmp$drug == "cefiderocol" & ft_cmp$matrix == "plasma")])) <= 3,
  # Cefiderocol plasma runs 1-6 points low (see Assumptions and deviations);
  # a mis-transcribed volume, rate constant or unbound fraction moves the
  # middle MICs by 10 points or more.
  max(abs(ft_cmp$diff)) <= 8
)
```

# PKNCA validation

The paper reports fCmax and fAUC0-24 for tobramycin, the aminoglycoside whose
targets are concentration- and AUC-driven: 17.7 mg/L and 103 mg.h/L in plasma,
6.6 mg/L and 76 mg.h/L in ELF (Results). PKNCA computes Cmax and AUC0-24 for
the tobramycin profiles, and Cmax and the steady-state AUC over 16-24 h for the
beta-lactam profiles, which have no published NCA targets.

```{r pknca}
conc_df <- sim |>
  filter(!is.na(fconc)) |>
  mutate(fconc = pmax(fconc, 0)) |>
  select(id, time, fconc, treatment)

dose_df <- bind_rows(lapply(seq_len(nrow(regimens)), function(i) {
  r <- regimens[i, ]
  tibble(
    id = 1L,
    time = as.vector(outer(r$dose_times[[1]], (seq_len(r$n_cycles) - 1) * r$tau, "+")),
    amt = rep(r$dose_amts[[1]], r$n_cycles),
    treatment = r$treatment
  )
}))

conc_obj <- PKNCA::PKNCAconc(conc_df, fconc ~ time | treatment + id)
dose_obj <- PKNCA::PKNCAdose(dose_df, amt ~ time | treatment + id)

intervals <- bind_rows(
  tibble(
    treatment = c("tobramycin plasma", "tobramycin ELF"),
    start = 0, end = 24
  ),
  tibble(
    treatment = c("meropenem plasma", "meropenem ELF", "cefiderocol plasma", "cefiderocol ELF"),
    start = 16, end = 24
  )
) |>
  mutate(cmax = TRUE, auclast = TRUE)

nca_res <- PKNCA::pk.nca(PKNCA::PKNCAdata(conc_obj, dose_obj, intervals = as.data.frame(intervals)))

as.data.frame(nca_res) |>
  filter(PPTESTCD %in% c("cmax", "auclast")) |>
  select(treatment, start, end, PPTESTCD, PPORRES) |>
  pivot_wider(names_from = PPTESTCD, values_from = PPORRES) |>
  rename(
    Treatment = treatment, Start = start, End = end,
    "fCmax (mg/L)" = cmax, "fAUC (mg.h/L)" = auclast
  ) |>
  knitr::kable(digits = 2, caption = "PKNCA on the simulated free plasma and ELF profiles.")
```

## Comparison against published NCA

```{r nca-compare}
published <- tibble::tribble(
  ~treatment,          ~cmax, ~auclast,
  "tobramycin plasma", 17.7,  103,
  "tobramycin ELF",    6.6,   76
)

tob_res <- as.data.frame(nca_res) |>
  filter(grepl("^tobramycin", treatment), PPTESTCD %in% c("cmax", "auclast"))

cmp <- nlmixr2lib::ncaComparisonTable(
  simulated = tob_res,
  reference = published,
  by = "treatment",
  units = c(cmax = "mg/L", auclast = "mg*h/L"),
  tolerance_pct = 20
)
knitr::kable(
  cmp,
  caption = "Tobramycin free exposures over 0-24 h: simulated vs. Fratoni 2025 (Results). * differs by >20%."
)

sim_tob <- tob_res |>
  select(treatment, PPTESTCD, PPORRES) |>
  pivot_wider(names_from = PPTESTCD, values_from = PPORRES) |>
  left_join(published, by = "treatment", suffix = c("_sim", "_pub"))
stopifnot(
  # Measured differences are 1-3%; the 10% bound still fails on any
  # mis-transcribed volume, rate constant, dose or unbound fraction.
  all(abs(sim_tob$cmax_sim / sim_tob$cmax_pub - 1) < 0.10),
  all(abs(sim_tob$auclast_sim / sim_tob$auclast_pub - 1) < 0.10)
)
```

# Assumptions and deviations

- **Free vs. total plasma.** The paper does not say explicitly whether the
  plasma models were fitted to total or free concentrations. The tobramycin
  numbers settle it: with the Table 2 parameters, the 9 mg/kg first injection
  gives a total Cmax of about 23 mg/L, and 0.776 times that is the reported
  fCmax of 17.7 mg/L. The plasma models therefore predict TOTAL
  concentrations (`Cc`), and `Cu = fu * Cc` gives the free exposures the paper
  reports and plots.
- **The unbound fractions** come from the paper's own text: meropenem 8% and
  cefiderocol 31.6% murine binding (cited by the authors to DeRyke 2007 and
  Monogue 2017), and tobramycin 22.4% measured in this study. They are carried
  as fixed parameters because they are not part of the least-squares fit.
- **Separate plasma and ELF fits.** Table 3 defines the ELF parameters as the
  absorption rate constant "into ELF compartment" and the elimination rate
  constant "from ELF compartment", so each ELF model is its own one-compartment
  model driven by the subcutaneous dose with no link to plasma. The packaged
  ELF models follow that structure: the depot drains straight into `elf`. Use
  the plasma model to simulate plasma and the ELF model to simulate ELF; their
  doses go into separate model instances.
- **Apparent volumes.** Subcutaneous bioavailability was not estimated, so
  every volume is V/F.
- **Meropenem plasma flip-flop.** The meropenem plasma fit has Ka = 1.34 1/h
  and Kel = 27.13 1/h with V/F = 0.04 L/kg. A one-compartment first-order
  absorption model cannot distinguish this from Ka = 27.13, Kel = 1.34 and
  V/F = 0.81 L/kg (the same curve); the published assignment is kept.
- **No variability.** The fit is naive-pooled least squares. No between-animal
  variability or residual error model is reported, so the models carry no etas
  and a proportional residual SD held at zero.
- **Cefiderocol plasma %fT > MIC.** The simulated values run 1-6 percentage
  points below Table 5 (44% against 50% at an MIC of 16 mg/L, 10% against 16%
  at 32 mg/L). Rounding of the two-figure Table 2 values moves these by no more
  than 2 points, and the gap is not closed by any single plausible change; the
  paper's own Figure 2 shows a free peak of roughly 50 mg/L against about
  48 mg/L here. The parameters are kept as printed. The other three regimens
  reproduce Table 5 to within 3 points.
- **Averaging interval for Table 5.** The paper reports "average exposures"
  without naming the interval. The third 8 h interval (16-24 h) is used here;
  the first interval differs by at most 4 points.
- **Human comparator curves** (the red lines of Figures 1-3) come from the human
  regimens the authors targeted and are not part of these murine models.
- No correction notice for the paper was found in a EuropePMC search on
  2026-11-02.
